## /rebar-debug Phase 2 complete — fix VERIFIED MERGED; closing

**State note (surprise, reported):** on re-entering with a fresh worktree off `origin/main`, the fix was **already merged** — `origin/main` HEAD `36ae045f41c3` ("fix(io): JS-safe ns timestamps in export NDJSON") carries `rebar-ticket: a8db-dc3c-983a-40b0` (Change-Id `Iea69e9212af937c77873a3ef0bba8ca56e0acaf7`), i.e. it already passed `LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1` and was Submitted. Remaining actionable was the ticket close; I independently re-verified the merged change before closing rather than assuming.

**Fix (merged, mirrors e127 exactly).** Export byte-emit routed through the single js-safe choke point `rebar._mcp_errors.js_safe_dumps` (`src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py:175`); `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1→2; `export.schema.json` description documents the wire form. Import twin coerces `created_at`/`comments[].timestamp` provenance with `int()` via new `_coerce_ns` (`src/rebar/_io/_provenance.py`), accepting both the new decimal-STRING form and older bare-int exports → canonical `int`. Non-test diff ~38 lines (well under the 150-line file_impact/review-plan floor).

**Runtime replication (bug gone).** Independent check: a stored 19-digit ns (`1787975097502255001`) emits on the wire as the exact decimal STRING `"1787975097502255001"`; regex finds **0** bare ≥16-digit integer tokens; `_provenance` coerces the string back to the exact `int` (digit-exact, not float64 `…255000`). `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION == 2`.

**RED→GREEN + mutation teeth.** Landed oracle `tests/interfaces/io/test_export_ndjson_js_safe.py` (4 tests) is GREEN. Step-5 mutation in a macOS `sandbox-exec` jail (writes confined to worktree+scratch): reverting the emit to bare `json.dumps` returned **3/4 tests to RED** — `test_export_emits_no_uninteroperable_integer` (wire-form: "export put a bare number on the wire"), `test_export_timestamps_round_trip_exactly`, `test_export_import_round_trip_preserves_exact_ns` (digit-exact, not type-only) — restored → GREEN. Tests have teeth.

**Acceptance criteria — all met:** (1) policy = decimal-string wire + `int()` import coercion; (2) `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped + BREAKING in `CHANGELOG.md` + `docs/release-notes.md` + `docs/import-export.md`; (3) digit-exact `export|import` round-trip test; (4) structural pin `test_export_emits_no_uninteroperable_integer`.

**Step-7 parity census.** NAME THE RULE: "serialization of a ticket-state ns `time.time_ns()` timestamp to an external JSON consumer must use the js-safe decimal-string wire form outside `|n|>2^53-1`." Channel census of the ns-timestamp JSON family: CLI `--output json` = js-safe (e127, guarded by `scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py` over `src/rebar/_cli`); MCP = js-safe (e127/6fe7); library NDJSON export = **fixed here**. No `backup`/`dump` subcommand exists. Other `src/rebar` `json.dumps` sites are non-interop (canonical hashing, cache keys, LLM prompts, editor server, telemetry logs); `metrics/snapshot.py` `ts` is an ISO-8601 STRING (N/A). No remaining MISSING slot; export was the last bare-ns surface. Sibling `spherelike-oily-honeyeater` (structural guard for NEW CLI commands) already closed and explicitly scoped export out.

**Escalation check: none.** Sole in-repo consumer of export NDJSON is `rebar import` (fixed in-scope). `export.schema.json` already typed these `["integer","string"]` and states the projection may evolve without breaking consumers, so no external consumer has a hard bare-int dependency — no operator migration decision required.

**Attribution.** `--class=preexisting --caused-by=ab74-b205-72af-4ce1` (epic rule-swamp-pupil): `git blame -w -C -M` traced the bare-int emit to `6119c24dedcd` "feat(io): T2 — NDJSON export" (the commit that introduced `export_ndjson.py`), under epic P1.2 rule-swamp-pupil. Preexisting omission (export always emitted bare ints since introduction; no good→bad transition). Recorded explicitly on the close to override best-effort blame auto-derivation.

Closing `in_progress → closed`.
